## The question this category answers

> How do you let anonymous strangers borrow against posted collateral with no maturity, no underwriting and no recourse — and close them out before the collateral is worth less than the debt?

## The category residue the original lane recorded

The answer to the assigned question, plainly: Aave V3 and Compound V3 do not produce identical strings, but the differences the vocabulary records are peripheral facilities, and every difference that matters is invisible to it. Aave carries {Fl, Bs, Cd, Xm, Fd} that Compound lacks; Compound carries {Im, Sl} that Aave (mostly) lacks. Everything describing how a loan is opened, priced, monitored and closed — Pl, Ix, Rb, Ct, Ex, Li, Em, Up, Tg, Gp — is shared verbatim. Meanwhile the four things that actually distinguish these protocols in production (kinked-vs-per-market rate model; multi-asset shared pool vs single base asset; repay-liquidation vs absorb-then-sell; interest-bearing vs inert collateral) generate exactly zero symbol differences. So the vocabulary's resolution in lending is roughly 'is it a pool, and does it have a health check' — which every entry answers yes to. SparkLend is worse: its element set is a strict subset of Aave V3's, containing no symbol Aave lacks, because it is an Aave V3 fork. Across the category the dominant gaps are (1) the interest-rate model, absent and load-bearing in all six; (2) delegated risk curation, an $8.76B business with zero coverage; (3) the risk-parameter layer (caps, ceilings, e-mode, close factor); (4) credit delegation, reachable only via contested Cg; (5) protocol-to-protocol credit lines; (6) off-chain enforcement and custody for the Uc/institutional wing.

## Lane narrative

**Status: round-one research did not complete.** This is the only category without a research record. The agent has been nudged to write what it has rather than continue researching.

**What the section introduction must cover when it does.** Lending is the category whose members are most alike under the vocabulary and most different in production. The corpus finding to test: everything describing how a loan is opened, priced, monitored and closed is shared verbatim across the largest protocols, while the four things that actually distinguish them are invisible.

**The two findings this lane decides**, because two other categories have already found the same shapes and lending is the tiebreak:

- **The price of credit.** No element anywhere names a rate. Every member runs a utilisation curve and that is what they compete on. The CDP lane found *four distinct rate instruments* among five protocols; lending's evidence decides whether the rate gap is one gap or several.
- **The delegated allocation mandate.** A curator choosing exposures for other people's deposits under caps, a timelock and a performance fee. The yield lane found this shape over allocations and the CDP lane found it over interest rates, independently. Lending is where the third independent sighting would be, and three lanes converging would make it the best-evidenced finding of the run.
